Trump Files original description-context rescue

Work only records in this input. This is offline proposal work: never edit canonical/live data or write Neon. Preserve supplied text, facts, exact URLs, IDs (including expanded IDs), and provenance. Inspect the staged row, frozen original when present, exact blocker, held204 terminal result when present, and supplied source URLs before deciding whether one focused rescue can resolve the gap. Do not add unrelated events, unsupported scoring, invented detail, filler, or broad research. At most ONE focused context rescue per record.

Return one append-only result per input record with the exact record_id and a terminal outcome: pass, hold, or exclusion_candidate. If pass, provide source-grounded reader-facing title, short, medium, and long descriptions; preserve adequate existing text. Limits: title <=180 characters; short <=180 characters; medium 45-90 words; long 140-300 words. No truncation or padding. Map each consulted URL to the facts it supports. A hold must state the precise remaining evidentiary/context gap. exclusion_candidate must explain why the record is not a discrete supported Trump event/action; it is a proposal only. Never turn a prior held204 release-ready flag into approval.

Suggested terminal JSON fields: record_id, outcome, proposed_title, proposed_description_short, proposed_description_medium, proposed_description_long, focused_rescue, sources_consulted (URL plus supported facts/limitations), remaining_gap, exclusion_reason, provenance. Keep output append-only and preserve input/history.

frozen_original.suggested_source_query: trump teacher tenure elimination union protection destruction public education workforce project 2025
frozen_original.synopsis: Donald Trump implemented Project 2025's systematic destruction of public education by eliminating teacher tenure protections, 'severely weakening and possibly banning' public sector unions, and creating legal mechanisms that allowed employers to 'end public employee unions in the middle of their contracts' while facilitating retaliation against educators who opposed ideological curriculum mandates. The comprehensive education workforce attack represented Trump's strategy to transform teaching from protected profession into at-will employment vulnerable to political pressure, eliminating job security that had enabled educators to maintain professional standards, academic freedom, and resistance to political interference in classroom instruction. The teacher protection elimination included allowing states to 'ban labor unions altogether' while creating loopholes that enabled school districts to terminate union contracts without cause, ignore federal minimum wage requirements, and eliminate overtime protections that had provided basic employment security for education workers. Trump's union destruction violated collective bargaining rights by enabling employer retaliation against union organizers while removing legal protections that had prevented political firing of teachers who refused to implement ideological mandates, teach censored curricula, or participate in discriminatory practices against students. The education workforce targeting created what teacher organizations called 'decimation' of public education that would 'reverse decades of civil rights protections' while making college education 'more inequitable and unaffordable' through systematic elimination of experienced educators and professional teaching standards. The teacher tenure elimination represented Project 2025's vision of education controlled by political loyalty rather than professional expertise, transforming public schools from centers of learning into ideological indoctrination systems where employment depended on conformity to conservative agenda rather than educational competence or student welfare.
frozen_original.title: Teacher Tenure and Union Protection Elimination - Public Education Workforce Destruction

proposal.description_long: The linked item is identified in the supplied evidence notes as a University of Utah faculty-union analysis discussing possible effects of Project 2025 proposals on teacher tenure and public-sector unions. That narrower framing describes a warning about proposals; it does not establish that the proposals became law or that protections were eliminated nationwide. The much broader original description asserted that Donald Trump had already dismantled tenure, canceled union contracts, enabled retaliation, and removed wage protections. The packet provides no federal enactment or state-by-state implementation record to support those claims. The linked union page returned 404 in the prior source check, so its full text and the specific Project 2025 provisions cannot now be independently reviewed from the supplied URL. This draft therefore attributes only the proposal-focused subject recorded in the evidence notes and avoids repeating the unsupported implementation language. Before adding examples, quotations, jurisdictions, or effects on educators, an accessible copy of the union analysis and the underlying proposal text should be checked. The evidence supports a limited account of what the analysis discussed, not a finding that the forecast consequences occurred.

supported_facts: The archived article is dated October 13, 2024 and titled ‘AFT: Project 2025 would decimate unions, public higher ed.’
It calls Project 2025 a to-do list for Trump ‘if he is elected president’ and says public-sector unions ‘would be severely weakened and possibly banned’ under the plan.
The article introduces the described effects with ‘If enacted, Project 2025 would’ and attributes discussion of potential effects to an American Federation of Teachers study.
The article describes potential effects on public-sector unions, academic freedom, and higher education; it does not mention teacher tenure.
source_fact_map.limitations: This is a forecast about a proposal, not evidence that any listed provision was enacted or implemented. It does not identify a specific law, order, implementing official, jurisdiction, changed tenure rule, or affected union contract.
